originalTitle: New free repair shop to launch in Oxford
summary: Organisers hope the initiative will attract enough interest to continue on a monthly basis.
content:
Repair of bikes and electrical items, as well as sewing, will be available on Saturday at St Barnabas Primary

Free help with repairing bikes, electrical items, computers and clothes is coming to an Oxford neighbourhood.

On Saturday, the first Jericho Repair Shop will take place at St Barnabas CE Primary School, in Jericho, between 10 and 12:00 BST.

Organiser John Mair said everyone was welcome to come along and donations would go back into rental costs and advertising for the event, which he hoped would continue on a monthly basis.

He said an initiative such as the repair shop "stops people throwing things away".

Mair said he decided to start a repair shop in Jericho after having used the service himself.

"I went to the repair shop in Wolvercote maybe a year or two ago and they repaired my garden blower - I thought this is a good idea," he said.

"I've brought over the man who repairs bicycles in Wolvercote, people who repair sewing, people who do computers, who sharpen knives."

Co-ordinator of Share Oxford, which also runs repair cafes in Oxford, Ben Tuppen previously said society needed to be more innovative in its approach to sustainability.

He also said they "were pleased to share how we run things and promote John's new repair café with our volunteers, some of whom have joined his team too".

Mair said: "If it doesn't work, repair it, don't throw it away and certainly don't throw it on the pavement."

Mair said he was looking forward to the launch and expected "anywhere between 10 and 100 people".

"It costs you nothing, but we'll expect a donation," he said.

"If enough people turn up, it'll be the first Saturday of November, and if enough people turn up, first Saturday of December."

Mair, who has been organising public events in Jericho such as Lazy Saturday and Lazy Sunday in Mount Place , said he wanted to see "how much demand there is".

He added: "All communities need hubs and this might as well be one, so why not?"

chineseTitle: 新的免费维修店将在牛津开业
chineseSummary: 组织者希望该倡议能够吸引足够的兴趣，以便每月继续进行。
chineseContent:
周六，圣巴拿巴小学将提供自行车和电器维修以及缝纫服务

牛津的一个社区将获得免费维修自行车、电器、电脑和衣服的帮助。

周六，第一家 Jericho 维修店将于英国夏令时 10:00 至 12:00 之间在 Jericho 的 St Barnabas CE 小学举行。

组织者约翰·梅尔表示，欢迎所有人前来参加，捐款将用于支付活动的租金和广告费用，他希望这种活动能够每月继续下去。

他说，像修理店这样的举措“可以阻止人们扔掉东西”。

梅尔说，他自己使用过这项服务后，决定在杰里科开设一家维修店。

“大约一两年前，我去了沃尔弗科特的修理店，他们修理了我的花园鼓风机 - 我认为这是个好主意，”他说。

“我请来了沃尔弗科特的修理自行车的人、修理缝纫的人、做电脑的人、磨刀的人。”

Share Oxford 的协调员 Ben Tuppen 此前也在牛津经营维修咖啡馆，他表示，社会在可持续发展方面需要更具创新性。

他还表示，他们“很高兴与我们的志愿者分享我们的经营方式和推广约翰的新维修咖啡馆，其中一些人也加入了他的团队”。

梅尔说：“如果不起作用，就修理它，不要扔掉它，当然也不要把它扔在人行道上。”

Mair 表示，他对此次发布充满期待，预计“人数在 10 到 100 人之间”。

“这不需要花费任何费用，但我们希望得到捐款，”他说。

“如果有足够多的人来，那就是十一月的第一个星期六，如果有足够多的人来的话，那就是十二月的第一个星期六。”

梅尔一直在杰里科组织公共活动，例如在蒙特普莱斯举办的“慵懒周六”和“懒惰周日”活动，他说他想看看“有多少需求”。

他补充道：“所有社区都需要中心，这也可能是一个中心，所以为什么不呢？”
